::: {.callout-important}
#### This is an example report used for teaching purposes

This is an example report used to help students understand how different types of report can be created using the Quarto markup language and the R programming language. **This contents of this report should not be relied upon for operational use.**
:::


```{r setup}
#| include: false

# Load packages ----
pacman::p_load(ggspatial, patchwork, scales, sf, tidyverse)



# Load data ----


## Incidents of illegal waste dumping ----

# This dataset does not contain the co-ordinates of each incident, only the name
# of the suburb in which it occurred. Therefore to map the data we will need to
# aggregate the incidents to suburbs and count the number in each suburb.
# Source: https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/yarra-dumped-waste
waste <- read_csv("https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/a03ae98f-da63-4669-9abf-fef9947b666a/resource/467fcec1-fd07-407a-ae19-790262d2d6c7/download/yarra-dumped-waste.csv") |> 
  # Keep only those rows representing incidents in 2018. Note that the `date`
  # column stores dates as a numeric value in YYYYMMDD format.
  filter(between(date, 20180101, 20181231), !is.na(suburb)) |> 
  mutate(
    # Harmonise spelling of suburb name to facilitate joining with the boundaries
    suburb = str_to_title(suburb),
    # Where `waste_type` contains multiple values separated by ';', replace 
    # those values with 'Multiple waste types'
    # `volume_m3` is stored as text, so convert this to a number
    volume_m3 = parse_number(volume_m3),
    waste_type = case_when(
      str_detect(waste_type, "\\;") ~ "Multiple waste types", 
      TRUE ~ waste_type
    )
  )


## Boundaries of suburbs in the state of Victoria ----

# Source: https://data.gov.au/dataset/ds-dga-af33dd8c-0534-4e18-9245-fc64440f742e/details?q=suburb%20boundary
suburbs <- read_sf("https://data.gov.au/geoserver/vic-suburb-locality-boundaries-psma-administrative-boundaries/wfs?request=GetFeature&typeName=ckan_af33dd8c_0534_4e18_9245_fc64440f742e&outputFormat=json") |> 
  mutate(vic_loca_2 = str_to_title(vic_loca_2)) |> 
  select(vic_loca_2, geometry)


# Wrangle data ----

waste_counts <- waste |> 
  # Count the number of incidents in each suburb and the total volume of waste
  # dumped
  summarise(
    incidents = n(), 
    volume = sum(volume_m3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .by = suburb
  ) |> 
  # Join boundaries
  left_join(suburbs, by = join_by(suburb == vic_loca_2)) |> 
  # Convert to an SF object (no arguments needed because R can extract the
  # necessary information from the existing `geometry` column in the data)
  st_as_sf() |> 
  # Convert to local co-ordinate reference system
  st_transform("EPSG:7899")

waste_counts_type <- waste |> 
  # Convert all but the most-common four types of waste into 'other'
  mutate(waste_type = fct_lump_n(waste_type, n = 5)) |> 
  # Count the number of incidents of each type in each suburb and the total 
  # volume of waste dumped
  summarise(
    incidents = n(), 
    volume = sum(volume_m3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .by = c(suburb, waste_type)
  ) |> 
  # Some suburbs might have zero counts for some types of waste. These will be
  # missing from the summarised data, so we add them back in with `complete()`.
  complete(suburb, waste_type, fill = list(incidents = 0, volume = 0)) |> 
  # Join boundaries
  left_join(suburbs, by = join_by(suburb == vic_loca_2)) |> 
  # Add rank of each suburb in terms of volume of waste
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(volume)), .by = waste_type) |> 
  # Convert to an SF object (no arguments needed because R can extract the
  # necessary information from the existing `geometry` column in the data)
  st_as_sf() |> 
  # Convert to local co-ordinate reference system
  st_transform("EPSG:7899")
```


This report identifies the parts of the City of Yarra that had the highest volume of illegal waste dumping in 2018. Incidents are recorded by the city authorities if the incidents are reported to them by other agencies or directly by members of the public. It is likely that the number of recorded incidents underestimates the actual number of incidents that occur, since not all land owners will report to the City authorities and some dumping may occur on land without a clear owner or manager who might report it.


```{r median-volume}
# We will save this to an object because we need the result twice: once to 
# report the value itself and once to work out whether 'metres' should be
# singular or plural

median_volume <- median(pull(waste, "volume_m3"))

yarra_population <- 91543
```


In 2018 there were `r comma(nrow(waste))` incidents of illegal dumping of waste in Yarra, with `r comma(sum(pull(waste_counts, "volume")))` cubic metres of waste being reported as dumped. The population of Yarra is approximately `r comma(yarra_population, accuracy = 100)`, indicating that in 2018 there was one reported dumping of illegal waste for every `r number(yarra_population / nrow(waste), accuracy = 0.1)` residents.

The typical incident involved only a small quantity of waste, with half of reported incidents involving `r median_volume` cubic `r if_else(median_volume == 1, "metre", "metres")` of waste or less and no incidents involving more than `r max(pull(waste, "volume_m3"))` cubic metres of waste.


```{r top-suburbs}
top_suburbs <- waste_counts |> 
  mutate(
    # Calculate the proportion of waste dumped in each suburb
    prop = volume / sum(volume),
    # Construct a suitable label for each suburb
    label = str_glue("{suburb} ({percent(prop, accuracy = 1)})")
  ) |> 
  # Keep only the three suburbs with the highest volume of dumped waste
  slice_max(order_by = volume, n = 3) |> 
  mutate(
    # Add some extra context to the first label
    label_long = if_else(
      row_number() == 1, 
      str_replace(label, "\\)", " of all the waste dumped in Yarra)"), 
      label
    ),
    row = row_number(),
    # Add version of labels with row number included
    label_num = str_glue("{ordinal(row)}. {label}")
  )
```


@fig-suburb-map shows the overall volume of illegal waste dumped in each suburb of Yarra in 2018. The `r nrow(top_suburbs)` suburbs with the highest volume of illegal waste dumping (out of the `r nrow(waste_counts)` suburbs in the city) accounted for `r percent(sum(pull(top_suburbs, "prop")), accuracy = 1)` of all reported illegal dumping in Yarra. Those suburbs were `r knitr::combine_words(pull(top_suburbs, "label_long"), oxford_comma = FALSE)`.


```{r suburb-map}
#| label: fig-suburb-map
#| fig-asp: 1
#| fig-cap: "Volume of illegal waste dumped in Yarra suburbs, 2018"
#| out-width: "100%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# This code produces a warning because `geom_sf_label()` produces slightly 
# misaligned labels when using lat/lon data, but this misalignment is nowhere
# near big enough to worry about.

ggplot(waste_counts) +
  # Add base map
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 1, progress = "none") +
  # Add volume
  geom_sf(aes(fill = volume), alpha = 0.7, colour = "grey25") +
  # Add suburb names
  geom_sf_label(
    aes(label = str_to_upper(str_wrap(suburb, width = 10))), 
    alpha = 0.5,
    colour = "grey25", 
    label.size = NA,
    lineheight = 1,
    size = 2.25
  ) +
  # Control scale showing number of incidents
  paletteer::scale_fill_paletteer_c(
    "ggthemes::Green", 
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  # Add labels
  labs(
    caption = "Data from City of Yarra, Geoscape Australia and OpenStreetMap",
    fill = "volume of\ndumped waste,\ncubic metres"
  ) +
  # Remove unnecessary supporting elements
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    # Give the legend a semi-transparent background
    legend.background = element_rect(colour = NA, fill = rgb(1, 1, 1, 0.75)),
    # Move legend to the right-hand side of the map
    legend.justification = c(1, 0),
    legend.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.15)
  )
```


It is not possible with the available data to identify where within each suburb dumping incidents were most concentrated. Further analysis would be necessary to identify the streets or open spaces with most incidents, but @fig-nbhd-maps shows the boundaries of the three suburbs that had the highest volume of dumped waste. 


```{r top-suburbs-map}
#| label: fig-nbhd-maps
#| fig-asp: 1
#| fig-cap: "Boundaries of the neighbourhoods with the highest volume of illegally dumped waste, 2018"
#| out-width: "100%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Make a map showing where the top suburbs are
locator_map <- ggplot(top_suburbs) +
  # Add base map
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0) +
  # Add all suburb boundaries
  geom_sf(data = waste_counts, colour = "grey25", fill = NA) +
  # Add top suburb boundaries
  geom_sf(alpha = 0.2, colour = "red3", fill = "red3", linewidth = 1) +
  # Add top suburb numbers
  geom_sf_label(
    aes(label = ordinal(row)), 
    alpha = 0.75,
    colour = "grey25", 
    label.size = NA,
    lineheight = 1,
    size = 2.25
  ) +
  # Make map cover a square area
  fixed_plot_aspect(ratio = 1) +
  # Remove unnecessary map elements
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "white", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
  )

# Create a function that takes a one-row SF object containing the outline of a
# suburb and then makes a map showing that boundary
top_suburb_map <- function(suburb_data) {
  
  # Create a mask around each suburb that will cover all the area of the map
  # *except* the suburb itself
  cutout <- suburb_data |> 
    # Put a 10km buffer around each suburb
    st_buffer(10000) |> 
    # Cut out the area of the suburb from the buffer area
    st_difference(suburb_data)
  
  ggplot(suburb_data) +
    # Add base map
    annotation_map_tile(type = "osm", zoomin = 0) +
    # Add mask
    annotation_spatial(data = cutout, alpha = 0.6, fill = "white") +
    # Add top suburbs boundary
    geom_sf(colour = "red3", fill = NA, linewidth = 1) +
    labs(subtitle = pluck(suburb_data, "label_num", 1)) +
    # Make map cover a square area
    fixed_plot_aspect(ratio = 1) +
    # Remove unnecessary map elements
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      panel.border = element_rect(colour = "white", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
    )
  
}

# Create map for each suburb and combine it with the locator map
wrap_plots(
  locator_map, 
  top_suburb_map(slice(top_suburbs, 1)),
  top_suburb_map(slice(top_suburbs, 2)),
  top_suburb_map(slice(top_suburbs, 3)),
  ncol = 2
) +
  # Add common caption at the bottom of all the maps
  plot_annotation(
    caption = "Data from City of Yarra, Geoscape Australia and OpenStreetMap",
  )
```


```{r waste-type-counts}
#| include: false

waste_type_counts <- waste_counts_type |> 
  # Convert from SF to tibble to make `count()` faster
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  # Calculate total volume of waste of each type
  count(waste_type, wt = volume, sort = TRUE) |> 
  mutate(
    # Calculate proportion of waste that was of each type
    prop = n / sum(n), 
    # Construct text showing each type and proportion
    label = str_glue(
      "{str_to_lower(waste_type)} ({percent(prop, accuracy = 1)})"
    )
  )
```


Dumped waste was categorised into several types: `r knitr::combine_words(pull(waste_type_counts, "label"), oxford_comma = FALSE)`. There was some variation in where different types of waste were dumped. @fig-type-maps shows the volume of waste of each main type that were reported as being dumped in each suburb. For example, while the suburb of `r pluck(slice_max(filter(waste_counts_type, waste_type == "General waste"), order_by = volume, n = 1), "suburb")` had the highest volume of dumping of general waste, `r pluck(slice_max(filter(waste_counts_type, waste_type == "Multiple waste types"), order_by = volume, n = 1), "suburb")` had the highest volume of dumping that involved multiple waste types.


```{r types-map}
#| label: fig-type-maps
#| fig-asp: 1.4
#| fig-cap: "Volume of illegal waste of different types dumped in Yarra suburbs, 2018"
#| out-width: "100%"

waste_counts_type |> 
  mutate(total_volume = sum(volume), .by = waste_type) |> 
  mutate(
    prop = total_volume / sum(volume),
    waste_type_label = fct_reorder(
      str_glue("{waste_type} ({percent(prop, accuracy = 1)})"), 
      total_volume, 
      .desc = TRUE
    )
  ) |> 
  group_split(waste_type_label) |> 
  map(function(type_data) {
    
    ggplot(type_data) +
      # Add base map
      annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
      # Add volume
      geom_sf(aes(fill = volume), alpha = 0.7, colour = "grey25") +
      # Add top suburb numbers
      geom_sf_label(
        aes(label = ordinal(rank)),
        data = slice_max(type_data, order_by = volume, n = 3),
        alpha = 0.75,
        colour = "grey25", 
        label.size = NA,
        lineheight = 1,
        size = 2.25
      ) +
      # Control scale showing number of incidents
      paletteer::scale_fill_paletteer_c(
        "ggthemes::Green", 
        labels = scales::label_comma()
      ) +
      # Add labels
      labs(
        subtitle = pluck(type_data, "waste_type_label"),
        fill = NULL
      ) +
      # Make map cover a square area
      fixed_plot_aspect(ratio = 1.2) +
      # Remove unnecessary map elements
      theme_void() +
      theme(
        # Give the legend a semi-transparent background
        legend.background = element_rect(colour = NA, fill = rgb(1, 1, 1, 0.75)),
        # Make legend key smaller
        legend.key.height = unit(0.75, "lines"),
        legend.key.width = unit(0.75, "lines"),
        # Make legend text smaller
        legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
        # Move legend to the bottom-right corner of the map
        legend.justification = c(1, 0),
        legend.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 3),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.02),
        # Add small white border to seprate maps
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "white", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
      )
    
  }) |> 
  wrap_plots(ncol = 2) +
  # Add common caption at the bottom of all the maps
  plot_annotation(
    caption = "Data from City of Yarra, Geoscape Australia and OpenStreetMap",
  )
```
